title: Make it yours
goal: Own your Neovim config: Lua instead of Vimscript, your own leader mappings, sane options, and a modern plugin manager with a fuzzy finder.

lessons.title: Your config in Lua: init.lua

concepts.desc: Lua entry point. Neovim refuses to start cleanly if init.vim and init.lua both exist.
Lua for `set x=v`. Booleans: vim.opt.number = true. Lists: vim.opt.clipboard = 'unnamedplus'.
plain option access: global / buffer-local / window-local values.
run Vimscript from Lua. Handy while you migrate piece by piece.
diagnose your setup (providers, clipboard, plugins).
show an option's value / and which file last set it.

lessons.tip: Migrate in small steps and restart often. If startup breaks, `nvim --clean` gives you a working editor to fix the config with.

quiz.q: What is the Lua equivalent of `set expandtab`?
Where does Neovim look for a Lua config on Linux?
What happens if both init.vim and init.lua exist?
quiz.a: Neovim reports a conflicting-configs error (E5422) and loads only one of them. Keep just one.

quiz.q: How do you run a line of Vimscript from Lua?
How do you find out which file last set 'tabstop'?
Your config is broken and nvim errors on start. How do you open nvim without it?

lessons.title: Leader key and mappings

concepts.desc: make Space your leader. Set it before any mapping that uses <leader>.
create a mapping. Non-recursive by default. opts: { desc = '...', silent = true }.
run a command from a mapping without changing mode or flashing the command line.
clear search highlighting until the next search. A classic <Esc> mapping.
list mappings (all / normal-mode ones starting with leader).
show a mapping and where it was defined.

lessons.tip: Map things you do dozens of times a day, under a mnemonic: <leader>w write, <leader>q quit, <leader>f... find. Use `desc` so the mappings document themselves.

quiz.q: Make Space the leader key in Lua.
Map <leader>w in normal mode to save the file.
Why put mapleader at the very top of init.lua?
quiz.a: <leader> is resolved when a mapping is defined. Mappings made before mapleader is set use the old leader (backslash).

quiz.q: Why use <cmd>...<CR> rather than :...<CR> in a mapping?
quiz.a: <cmd> runs the command directly: no mode change, no command-line flash, and it works the same in any mode.

quiz.q: How do you see where a normal-mode mapping for `gx` was defined?
Is vim.keymap.set recursive (like :map) or not (like :noremap) by default?
quiz.a: Non-recursive (noremap) by default. Pass { remap = true } to change that.

lessons.title: Options and autocommands that pay off

concepts.desc: line numbers relative to the cursor, so counts like 7j or d4k need no arithmetic.
keep 8 lines of context above and below the cursor.
keep undo history after closing the file.
searches ignore case unless you type an uppercase letter.
new splits open to the right / below, where you're looking.
run code on events. TextYankPost + vim.hl.on_yank() briefly highlights what you yanked.
group autocmds so re-sourcing the config doesn't duplicate them.

lessons.tip: Relative numbers plus counts beat hjkl spam: look at the gutter, type 6↓ (or 6j). That's two keys, every time.

quiz.q: With ignorecase and smartcase on, does /Foo match `foo`?
quiz.a: No. An uppercase letter in the pattern makes the search case-sensitive.

quiz.q: What does 'scrolloff' do?
quiz.a: Keeps that many lines visible above and below the cursor when scrolling.

quiz.q: Which option keeps undo history after you close and reopen a file?
Which event fires after a yank, and which function highlights the yanked text?
Why put autocmds in an augroup with clear = true?
quiz.a: Re-sourcing the config then replaces them instead of adding duplicates.

quiz.q: Which two options make :split open below and :vsplit open to the right?

lessons.title: lazy.nvim and telescope

concepts.desc: plugin manager: bootstrap it from init.lua, then list plugins as specs, e.g. { 'nvim-telescope/telescope.nvim', dependencies = {...} }.
plugin UI: install (I), update (U), sync (S), profile startup (P).
fuzzy-find files by name in the current project.
search file contents as you type (uses ripgrep).
jump between open buffers / search :help.
next/previous result; open the result in a split / vsplit.

lessons.tip: Neovim 0.12 also has a built-in plugin manager, vim.pack (:help vim.pack). lazy.nvim is still the most common choice in examples, so it's the one you learn first.

quiz.q: Which command opens lazy.nvim's UI?
Which external tool does telescope's live_grep need?
Write a mapping: <leader>ff runs telescope find_files.
In a telescope picker, how do you open the selected file in a vertical split?
Where does lazy.nvim install plugins by default?
How do you see which plugins slow down startup?
quiz.a: :Lazy profile (or P in the :Lazy UI); also nvim --startuptime file.log

lessons.title: Week 10 review: Vimscript to Lua, fast

concepts.desc: capture groups turn repetitive config lines into Lua in one command.
→ vim.opt.x = true / vim.opt.x = v
→ vim.keymap.set('n', 'lhs', 'rhs')
regex: a run of non-space characters / of word characters.

lessons.tip: When a dozen lines need the same change, write one substitution (or one macro), not twelve edits.

quiz.q: Convert every `set foo` line (no value) into `vim.opt.foo = true` with one command.
Lua: map Esc in normal mode to clear search highlighting.
Lua: turn on relative line numbers.
What does \S\+ match in a Vim regex?
Which command shows lazy.nvim's plugin list and status?
Which built-in function briefly highlights yanked text?
